title: Eviction-policy misapplication causes silent cold-starts and tenant throttling
creator: Asha Patel
description:
Summary: ACME Travel reported intermittent high tail latency and a spike of 429/503 responses during a weekday traffic peak. Symptoms were confined to the tenant's dedicated reserved pool where callers experienced silent 'cold starts' (requests routed to cold workers or queued without visible allocation) and burst-rate rejections despite apparent available capacity.

Investigation established that a recent allocator change intended to make pool eviction decisions more aggressive under memory pressure incorrectly treated recently-prefetched 'hot' slots as candidates for eviction when their backing container had a transient scheduling annotation. The result was a small but steady leak of hot slots from mid-sized reserved pools (10-50 GPUs) that depleted burst headroom over multiple minutes, triggering internal fallback to cold pools and tenant-level throttling before autoscaler could replenish slots.

Root cause: a race between the pool-eviction controller and the prefetch reconciler where the eviction controller consulted stale slot metadata (eviction_timestamp > prefetch_timestamp) due to missing consistent reads from the allocator store. The allocator then moved slots to general free lists instead of honoring tenant burst reservations.

Resolution: Patch allocator to use authoritative slot state (use single-source-of-truth index), add a lease-check before eviction, and tighten burst-accounting invariants so reclaimed headroom is reflected in the autoscaler sensor immediately. Backported fix to controller-2.4 and runtime-1.19 (hotfix branch).

Rollout: staged canary across one region then global. Monitoring and rollback hooks added. Customer mitigations included a manual temporary headroom grant and a short-lived increase in burst quota while we verified the fix.

Follow-ups: updated runbook with precise mitigation steps, added a new alert (reserved_pool_hot_eviction_rate > 0.1% over 5m), tightened autoscaler scale-up thresholds, and created a small test harness to simulate prefetch/evict races in CI.

2025-02-20 13:20 - Initial hypothesis: autoscaler overshot scale-down when ephemeral scheduling glitches occurred. Found eviction logs showing hot-slot evictions with no corresponding container failures.

2025-02-21 14:40 - Root cause found: allocator reads stale slot metadata because prefetch reconciler writes were not serialized with eviction reads. Patch prepared to add lease check and canonical index read.
2025-02-22 03:12 - Hotfix PR raised: https://github.com/redwood/allocator/pull/13487. Patch includes unit-tests and an integration test that reproduces the race under controlled timing.
2025-02-22 08:00 - Canary rollout started in us-west-2 (10% traffic). No regression observed in canary after 90m. Proceeded to region-wide rollout with monitoring.

2025-02-23 01:10 - Backports applied to release branches: runtime-1.19-hotfix and controller-2.4-hotfix. QA signed off on both backports.
2025-02-24 18:30 - Post-deployment checks: reserved_pool_hot_eviction_rate alert stayed at zero, tenant burst headroom delta normalized. Collected 72h of telemetry for the postmortem.

release_notes: Fixed allocator eviction race that could deplete burst headroom for reserved pools, causing silent cold starts and tenant throttling. Backported to runtime-1.19 and controller-2.4.
